intended_object: The resolution theorem for K₀ of exact categories, in its projective form. If 𝒫 is a full subcategory of E-projective objects that contains zero and is closed under biproducts, the inclusion of 𝒫 into the subcategory of objects with a finite 𝒫-resolution induces an isomorphism K₀(𝒫) ≅ K₀(objects with a finite 𝒫-resolution). The inverse sends [X] to the alternating sum Σ(−1)ⁱ[Pᵢ] over any such resolution. This is read off the docstring and the name.
explanation:
The forward map is the canonical map `ExactK0.map` induced by the exact inclusion functor 𝒫 ⊆ admitsFiniteResolution 𝒫, which is exactly the map in the classical theorem. The inverse is `eulerHom`, the lift of the Euler-characteristic invariant. Both inverse laws are proved on generators, so the definition really is the claimed isomorphism, and its underlying map is the natural one.

The hypotheses are standard. 𝒫 ⊆ projectives, contains zero and is closed under binary products. Together these make 𝒫 replete and extension-closed, because a conflation ending in a projective object splits. Fixing the universe w (with smallness assumptions) is a technical requirement for K₀ to be a set-sized group. It does not restrict the mathematics.

A more general resolution theorem, for resolving subcategories, exists separately in the library (TauCeti/CategoryTheory/GrothendieckGroup/Resolving.lean). The projective-resolution version is itself a standard statement in the literature, so this is a legitimate variant rather than a needlessly narrow one.

Mathlib has no Grothendieck group of exact categories, so there is no counterpart.
